# Chapter Two: Northern Dominance

Corliss stood on the squat ramparts and surveyed the fields to the north, the carts with the supplies were due back an hour ago she thought tensing as she thought of what might have happened to her fellow wardens. The entire squad no gone two days as they gathered the abandoned supplies and were set to head back using back trails to avoid soldiers.

“Do not fear mistress, it is still early for them to be returning” the gentle voice making her jump as the Silva leader General Erod Durass appeared from nowhere. The Silva moved like shadows she thought nodding to him “I know, just won’t be at east until I see them return” she answered him. Durass regarded the landscape with those large almond shaped eyes that she had been surveying, the moonlight sparkling in his deep emerald eyes “Except for the two foxes, the field is clear” he stated, and she looked again, not seeing the pair of supposed foxes. After spending some time with the Silva, she got the impression the eyes that were double the size of a normal human’s aloud them the ability to see further and in lower light then she herself could.

His dark green tinted hair giving him almost a otherworldly look when matched with his narrow face and slender frame. “I sent my very best warriors with them, they will not be surprised by the soldiers, these men are trained in stealth and each one a master marksman Mistress, they will be safe” he assured her, and Corliss nodded to him.

Durass had met them when they had reached this place, helping the wardens gather the wounded and transport them to the small abbey they now found themselves in. Looking out to the left and right of the small abbey Corliss could make out the tents of the stout mountain tribe and the Elven as they formed the broder army. Durass had brought his and the mountain dwarves down from the borderlands once it had been rumored the Empress meant to move against them.

They had met Uri and the wardens once they had reached the small abbey. There was a familiarity between Uri and this General Durass that had taken Corliss by surprise and now standing alone with the man on the ramparts she decided to find out what she could. “How long have you known Uri?” she asked casually but could see the smile spread across the man’s face, he had seen through the feeble attempt to gain information but seem to only acknowledge it before he answered her.

“The Lord Adjudicator is known to my people as he has been our contact with the outside world this was his task for taking part in convincing your people to accept the agreement between our two races. “ He had told her some of how the two of them had met, and she was about to ask him to tell the story in more detail when his arm stretched out and pointed towards the horizon, Corliss followed the extended arm and sighed with relief as the first of the supply wagon’s crested into sight.

She was at the gate to meet them when the Warden’s rode in “How was the trip?” she asked and the Warden who rode with the first cart shrugged and smiled “uneventful, we caught sight of a few patrols but were able to dodge them easily, we have all the supplies we left behind, and a few more refugees coming from some of the southern towns then his face fell “The stories aren’t good, Lord Amital should talk to them as soon as he has a chance” he finished and Corliss nodded, knowing she would see that done even before all the carts were in.

As the group continued to unload the carts as they entered the abbey’s small courtyard, she led a small group of dirty and battered refugees to the main building. It was not an impressive structure and only stood about twenty feet wide, the small open room inside had been turned into a headquarters and was Corliss entered she caught sight of Uri and a few of the Silva as they talked over maps that had been spread out across the table in the center of the room. “Uri, may I see you” she called motioning her mentor over.

He excused himself and the big man lumbered over to her, she could see the curious expression on his face as he looked over the refugees accompanying her. She motioned to the first of them “They were brought in with the wagons, apparently they are coming from some of the southern towns, they have news” she finished and Uri walked over grabbing a blanket off of one of the chairs, walking over to an older woman, he gently laid it on her shoulders and motioned for the group to follow.

After a few minutes of coordination, he had large pot of soup from lunch setup and heated for the small group and sat with them as they ate. Both he and Corliss sitting in silence as the man who seem to lead them went over the details that had led him north. “I am Justi Grumber, a farmer from the south, the town we live in isn’t a big one my Lord and Lord Seer Hurit had led us for many, many years and he was a good Lord you see. About a month ago soldiers showed up they did, with a new Seer” he began as Uri offered to refill the bowls of those finished with there soup “Go on Justi” Corliss prodded gently to the farmer. “This new Lord Seer was different, he dressed like a monk, covered in strange symbols he was and eyes as black as night my Lord, he gathered us up and made us watch as he killed Lord Seer Hurit, he had the powers of a Mage and creatures that he commanded like demons straight out of hell they were” he continued and Corliss could see the fear in everyone’s eyes as he described the demons and the new Lord Seer.

“He said we was to work for free, that the Empress demanded supplies for her armies and anyone who didn’t work would end up like the old Lord Seer, all our lands were taken from us my Lord, that night we ran, but he sent those white demons after us, only about half of us made it here” he finished and looked down shaking his head and Corliss could see the fresh tears that spilt from his eyes and down his cheeks “My wife didn’t make it, nor did my baby girl my Lord, the Empress is making slaves of us, how are we supposed to fight the Empress, and the mages?” he asked and she could hear the hopelessness in his voice. “You are safe here farmer, as are your people” Uri said gently laying a hand on the man’s shoulder. He nodded and a small appreciative smile spread across his face “Thank you my Lord” he whispered through the sobs of relief.

Uri and Corliss stepped over to the table, leaving the refugees to eat and rest. “By Aurtus what is happening Uri, the Empress has mage seer’s and some kind of creatures that they command?” she asked as if even she couldn’t believe she was saying it. Uri shook his head “We don’t know anything yet, just stories from frightened commoners” he finished making a calming gesture.

Corliss knew they would have to send out scouts, find out what was happening, if the Empress was turning her subjects into slaves then they had to know, this was unprecedented she thought her mind reeling at the implications. What of the mages, had they joined her? Corliss wondered remembering the stories of the Mage wars and of the churches attempt to annihilate anyone showing the gift. Corliss gathered the elder Wardens as Uri went and retrieved Durass and a few of his senior warriors. Standing in the small room the eight people present gathered around the small table, everyone looking serious as the stories the refugees had come in with quickly made their way through the ranks. “Everyone be calm we have to gain intelligence before we start assuming the accuracy of the stories, these are frightened people who is to know what of there stories are real or imagined” Durass stated as he looked around at the those gathered. “Ha, I never trusted the mages, who is to say they are not in league with the Empress and we all know she has been up to something for years, there has been rumors and talks of projects and experiments” Yorst a small rotund Warden said throwing Uri a challenging look, the two always seemed to be at odds thought Corliss, knowing there was something there that went beyond just simple rivalries had never understood the animosity between Uri and Yorst, and now was not the time to get into it she thought.

She could still not get over the odd look the Silva but had been getting better at not staring and gawking, at least she hoped she had. Everyone had heard the stories of the outcasts and how they were different from other people, the tribes who inhabited the barrens had never ventured out and few who saw them returned to talk about it.

But yet Uri knew at least one of them, she had never heard him speak of Durass or his people before, why had he kept that from her she wondered eyeing the tall slight General Durass.

Uri stepped forward nodding to Durass “We do, but our first priority Is to reinforce our defenses here, if the rumors are true an army is forming at our northern keep and the Empress means to march on the barrens as well.” He finished illiciting a nod from Durass. Corliss watching curiously, since showing up Durass had treated Uri with nothing but deference and respect, despite his position and the two to one warrior ratio he had over the wardens, she would have to find out what the story was behind there meeting she thought yet again.

“Lord Amital” Began Durass, his tone again with a hint of deference as he used Uri’s official rank in front of his people and the Senoir Wardens

“Say the word and I can have three legions of my best bowman here within a day and half” he responded.

Uri thought about it for a moment and then nodded “Do it, the more we have here, the better we can hold the line, while you are doing that I will have a scout contingent of my Wardens head out and see if we can’t find out more information about what’s going on out there” he said and nodded to Corliss who without a word, turned and left the room. As she walked out a voice called after her and she turned to see Durass coming up behind her. “I will also send a few of my bowman Warden, they will be of great help while you are scouting” he said and at first she thought about refusing the offer, but she had seen them move and hunt, Corliss had to admit they were incredible woodsman she swallowed her pride and nodded to the Silvan General “Of course, send two and with two wardens that will make the party small enough to move fast and get out if we find trouble” she said and he smiled at her nodding.

Corliss continued into the camp looking around until she found the two, she was looking for. Matest and Burin, fall in, you are volunteered for scout duty” she called, and the two men turned and smiled at her. In the wardens there was always competition in who could bring in the most fugitives, but it was all in fun and year after year these two had been the ones nipping at her heels for first place, who better to assist her then these two she thought as the two men walked over carrying the long rifles over there shoulder. “What are we hoping to find” the shorter of the two Matest asked, his bushy blonde beard hiding the boyish face that had gotten him teased as an initiate, but she could still see the mischievous twinkle in those blue eyes.

Burin a head taller than Matest nodded, his clean face and bald head a contrast to his compatriot “I take it we are taking the two elves who are coming this way?” he asked pointing behind Corliss. Without even turning around she nodded “We need to know whats happening, I don’t think we will have to go far, there are two towns within a days ride of this place, we are going to go by them and find out what we can and report back” she finished laying out the plan.

The men nodded as the two Silvan Bowman, stood regarding the approaching group, the ashwood longbows and curved gleaming short swords snugly attached to the leather straps that crossed there thin bronze chests, once they were all together, she briefed the group, noticing how the Wardens eyed the Silvan, who actively did there best to ignore there awe struck expressions. Corliss stifled a smile, glad she wasn’t the only one doing it.

The small group rode out within the hour, the Silvan taking the lead and scouting ahead for danger. Sunlight was just beginning to break over the trees by the time they ran into anything that resembled trouble. They stayed along the treeline taking the hunting trails when they could, as they crested a bend, they came upon the two Silvan both off there horses and motioning the small group to stop. Corliss slowed her horse, climbing down from it she unstrapped her pistols and ensuring the sword on her back was easily accessed as she approached the two, who still looked towards the south. “Report” she said one of the elven turning, they had never offered their names and she realized that she had not asked. Not finding a way that didn’t sound rude in her mind, she merely left it nodding to the closest one and waiting for him to speak.

“Bodies ahead, they are soldiers, but not the Empress’s, I think they are Lusor’s, we can’t be sure though didn’t want to get too close before we surveyed the area, it might be a trap” the closest one whispered. Corliss nodded in approval motioning for her two Warden’s to join her. “You two take the west” she said pointing to the Silvan bowmen “you two take the east, meet back here if don’t find anything, this is a look only, no engaging unless you don’t have a choice” she continued to whisper as the men set off, leaving Corliss alone, she crouched low and approached, keeping a good amount of treeline in front of her as she surveyed the bodies lying in the field beyond. Thirty minutes later the two groups made their way backing coming towards her on the opposite sides as to which they started, completing the recon circle. Once they were back and confirmed no soldiers the group slowly and cautiously made their way out to the bodies.

The Silvan spreading out, bows at the ready they stood watch as Corliss and the other wardens examined the damage. Approaching the first body he noticed the long gashes through the leaf pattern bronze armor on the chest. “What ever cut this man went through the metal like butter” she said looking over the soldier. The man’s eyes were still open and even in death she could see the abject fear on his face. Whatever had done this had scared this man almost to death.

Looking over the other bodies she noticed the same wounds, there were no resin shots or arrows, something had gotten in close and whatever it was, it had some damn sharp claws. Picking up the rifle she checked the chamber and found the round within, in fact none of the guns were fired. “Whatever did this came upon these guys fast, they had no time to pull their weapons or fire” she stated as Corliss began walking a circular pattern using the bodies as the centerpoint as she canvased the area for tracks or other items that might point to who did this. Then she found the first set, squatting over the ground Corliss ran her hand over what looked like a bare human foot, except it was just a little too long and she could make out what looked like indents from claws in front of the toes. “What in Aurtus’s name” she exclaimed calling the other two over. “What do you guys make of this?” she asked and both Burin and Matest looked confused as they studied the tracks and the Burin walked a little way finding another set. : The gate is too long, and look here, hand prints this one was on all fours” he finished and Corliss walked over to join him. Seeing the print, she could also see the quad gouges in the ground “Claws” she whispered, looking back at the bodies as the death scene began to clarify itself in her mind. “Whatever these were, they move too fast, come out of the darkness and were upon them before they realized there was a threat, they held no weapons and using claws strong enough to pierce bronze they cut the soldiers apart” she finished and then reflected on what she had just said.

“We need to go guys, now, if whatever this was is still out there I damn sure don’t want to meet it” she said and received grunts of agreement from the other two, The three got up and began moving back to the brushline of the woods “We have movement” one of the elven whispered just loud enough for them to hear. Corliss stopped in her tracks, surveying the direction the elven man was studying. Then she saw it as a splotch of white shot between trees about a hundred yards out. It was too far to make out any detail but whatever it was moved fast she thought, then another further down as bushes moved and she caught another white splotch as it passed by the brushline.

“We need to move, we do not want to be in the open guys” she said and Corliss turned sprinting back towards the woods, she could hear the footfalls as the two Silvan were on her heals. Then a scream rose from somewhere to there left, it curdled her blood as it rose to a cretiendo, another joining it, this one much closer. Cursing silently Corliss willed herself to put on more speed “What are you” she said and finally hit the brushline running past the two other wardens as she did. The first Silvan hit the trees and came to stand next to her, but as she watched the last man reached two steps within the woodline and something slammed into it from its right, taking the elven off his feet. Corliss could hear the two seconds of screaming before it ended in a phlegmy cough, then nothing.

Without though for herself Corliss burst from the treeline to see the shredded body but no attacker, the scream had ended only a moment ago but whatever it was, was already gone. “We need to move NOW” she screamed, turning and bursting back into the trees. They shot through the woods running as fast as they could, taking a turn around a tree Corliss came up short to find the carcasses of the four horses they had ridden in on laying on the ground where they had left them standing.

They are hunting us she thought, getting close to the tree and crouching down, slowly she pulled the mahogany hilt of the straight sword as she carefully surveyed the trees above. She could hear the other three fast approaching, putting her arm around the tree she flashed a hand sign and heard when they slowed and then quietly moved to the left and right of her. The tree branches were dark, with no direct moonlight it was next to impossible to see anything, but Corliss continued to slowly scan above. Then she caught movement to her left and looked up to see something skulk along a large branch, disappearing behind the trunk, it didn’t come out the other side and Corliss frantically looked up and down to see if it had changed elevation instead. As she surveyed the tree her breath caught in her chest as something landed directly to her right. Turning her head slowly she came face to face with the blue glowing eyes of a creature out of nightmares. Cocking its head it studied her, as if curious, it was about the size and shape of a man, but its skin was corpse white and its torso was elongated along with its arms and feet, giving it the ability to run on all fours she thought.

The creature stopped cocking its head and went tense for a moment, then with a high screech it reared back to pounce, Corliss shielded her face but nothing hit her, looking over her arm, she saw it laying on the ground an arrow buried deep in its skull, the eyes no longer glowed and the animal man thing just lay there twitching as it gave off its final death throes. The remaining elven appeared from behind a tree further down and walked over to the creature, pulling the arrow from its head and spitting on it. “That is for my brother, demon” he said. They both turned as further down they caught the wail of the other creature she had seen, but this was not a hunting scream, it was a wail of sorrow “It knows we killed its partner” she said and motioned for the others to join her a few moments later another wail floated over the air, but this one came from further away “Its leaving” she finished and realized she had been holding her breath. They waited root there to the spot, watching the trees above like prey animals awaiting the wolf. After a time, they moved, collecting the gear they could carry from the horses and packing the body of the thing the elven had killed and set out for the abbey.

It took most of the night and half the next day before they crested the rise to see the line of soldiers along each side of the ancient abbey. As they walked Corliss to the time to get to know her new ally. “So, I have to ask why is it you all look alike, similar the the mountain clan they seem to be their own species, I have never seen anything like it” she said doing her best not to insult the elven who had saved there life. He just smiled giving her a sideways glance. Ages ago the ancient who founded our land had the ability to manipulate genetics with his magic, it was an ability he had cultivated for decades, his abilities and knowledge as a scientist allowed him to take a small group of people and alter them in a way that created our races, there are three us, the dwarfs of the mountain and the ethereals, though the etherals tend to keep to themselves while the dwarves and Elven keep steward over the land. In fact, the ancient named our land after his god” he finished, and Corliss cocked her head curiously, “The ancients god was named Barren” she asked and the Silvan hunter tilted his head back and let out a loud belly laugh. “No, that is what you call our land, its actual name is Viridi” he finished, and Corliss nodded.

they continued to make their way to the abbey.

By the time they reached the gates, two of the wardens were coming out to meet them on horses. “What happened?” one called down, but Corliss dismissed it, instead handing him the rope to the large sack dragging behind her. “get this into the main building and wait for me” she said, happy to have the heavy bundle off of her shoulder. Corliss entered the keep finding Uri and Durass standing over the bundle and regarding it. Uri turned and smiled as she walked through the door “Whatever you brought, smells horrible my dear” he said as Corliss, without a word walked over and motioning the other two to help, hefted the bundle onto the table and unwrapped it.

Once they caught sight of what was under the cloth any joviality in their faces quickly washed away. “By Aurtus’s beard, what is that thing” Uri whispered looking the creature over. Corliss looked at the two men, from the looks on their faces neither of them had seen it before and that wasn’t good news. “I was hoping the Silvan had seen this before, but I guess they have not” she said illiciting a shrug from Durass. “I don’t know what it is, but it is fast and deadly, killed a whole squad of Turen soldiers before they could get off a shot” she said. “But if none of you have seen it, then its something new and with everything that has been going on in the territory it means either the Empress or the Mages have brought new weapons to the field of battle she finished. After they looked it over for nearly thirty minutes, Durass called in one of his healers and they left the body with them, while the three of them left the building to walk the perimeter and get some air. Truth be told, no one wanted to be present while the healer cut into the body. So they walked the line checking the defenses and discussing tactics as they did.

After an hour the group returned to find the healer standing outside the building and washing off the blood of the creature. “What can you tell us Durass asked her” The healer shook her head and winced at the question. It is like nothing I have ever seen, but I can tell you that it started its life as a normal human, probably was a young lady around seventeen when whatever this is happened to her, she was pregnant as well, but the trauma I am seeing looks as if she had lost the baby during the transformation process, but I can’t be sure” the healer said shaking her head and doing her best to keep the angry and disgusted look off of her face. “Whoever did this to that young girl, is a monster of the worst kind my Lords” she finished the statement hanging in the air between them. “What can you tell us about it, what is the creatures capabilities” Uri asked and the doctor nodded. Some of the bones have been extended and the muscle structure is definitely changed, this is a creature that is as comfortable running on all fours as it is on two legs, it has long sharp and durable claws on its hands for defense and climbing, the claws on the feet look to be only for traction on either a flat surface or aiding it in ascending. Teeth are sharp, but not long so more for eating then a weapon, however dissecting its corneas the creature can see in low light and normal light, however bright light will probably disorient it for a moment, it looks to have a normal human size brain, but this was buried into it, it wasn’t shoved in, but looks to have been surgically implanted” she finished brandishing an odd orange crystal about six inches long. “I don’t know what its purpose is, but whoever inserted used magic to weld it to the cranial bone so it wouldn’t slip out.” With that the doctor bowed to the three men and excused herself.

They watched her go as all three thought on what the woman had said. Entering the small building they found her assistants cleaning up the table after the dissection.

“So, who do we think made that thing” Corliss asked a shiver ran through her body as she remembered that creature moving through the woods. No one spoke for a moment and finally Uri broke the silence. “We know the Empress has been appointing new Lord Seer’s from the observations these are men with power, either mages that do not report to the order or something new” he said and Durass turned to regard him.

“How do we know they are not part of the order?” he asked though his tone was curious and not challenging so Uri shrugged “Because the tenants the order lives by, don’t kill with magic and every one of these bastards kill the old Lord Seer as an example to the common people of what will happen should they get out of line. That doesn’t sound like the order I know” he finished and Durass nodded. “Whoever created it, we will need to be vigilant, if the healer’s assumptions on how it moves are correct, this thing will not be easy to kill” The Silvan General offered as the group went back to reviewing the map. As they reviewed the defenses, making suggestions and notes on changes the front door burst open as an excited initiate came running into the room. “My Lords, a platoon has been seen on the horizon” he yelled with a quick now he rushed out of the room and the three generals followed quickly.

Making their way to the ramparts, Durass was the first to arrive, as they gathered Uri pulled out the farseer tube with the crystals on each end and began to examine the group of horsebacked soldiers. “They are Empress’s guard, but what are they doing this far north?” he asked. Corliss cursed silently “They probably found the soldiers from Turen and decided to do a patrol to see if there were more, whatever the reason, they have spotted us, now the question is what will they do. “Durass squinted looking out over the field “They are too few for an all out assault, but that doesn’t mean they won’t attack, Wardens Keep is only three days ride, they can have backup within the week” he proffered and both men nodded solemnly knowing the Silvan general had a point.

Keep the men active and watch them, lets see what they decide to do” Uri said, and the other men nodded in agreement as they turned and headed back into the small building. Before they could leave the ramparts, someone called out and pointed at the small group. Uri looked again and saw the three small carts moving forward, using the farseer he examined them and then putting it down handed it to Durass.

“They look like weapons but nothing I have ever seen before” he said and the Elven general took the proffered farseer, putting his eye to it, he looked out over the field at the odd thing they seemed to be setting it, it was a large metal tube on a wooden cart, the back of it long, as if it were made to lay on the ground as a brace. “The metal tub looks like a short barrel of some kind, is it a new gun, if so they are far back to use it, if the range from the muskets are any indication” he said returning the farseer to Uri. “Still, lets have the men take cover as best they can, if this is a weapon, I don’ t want to be caught surprised. There have been too many new things we have not seen before to easily dismiss this one my friends” he said, and both men nodded.

“Sage advice my Lord Duass said as he called two initiates over. “Get the men to fall back and take cover, tell them we expect an attack but are unsure of its nature” he finished, and the two initiates scrambled off. It was a mere two hours when they finally discovered the use of odd looking carts as they reviewed the area Durass setting up two squads of soldiers to perform flanking maneuvers should these soldiers attack a loud boom sounded from across the field, as all three looked up an arc of blue flame shot across the sky coming down just outside the ramparts, the explosion that followed cracked the ancient wall in four places sending mortar and stone flying into the camp. A few screams were heard as a few close to the wall were hit with the stone shrapnel.

“Get back, take cover”

Durass began to yell as he ran towards the wall, he never quite made it as a second blue arc of flame came down on the inside of the wall and Durass as thrown twenty feet into a line of tents as people began running and screaming, the blue flame blowing outward, like a liquid it splattered on the buildings and stuck there burning.

“Crystal fire” Uri breathed, get everyone as far back as possible, they are using crystal fire” he yelled, running to aid Durass as he began frantically coordinating the men. Pulling the Silvan general from the collapsed tents, Uri looked him over to find only a few scratches and bruises. “We have to move Durass” he exclaimed as the two of them bolted for the rear of the compound as Yorst headed towards the west to direct the troops to take cover. Another salvo of rounds beat into the courtyard of the old abbey as one section of wall collapsed. “We need to take the fight to them” Yorst screamed over the raging blue flames and Uri nodded. Durass made a motion of his hand and two of the young Silvan nodded gravely taking off.

As the soldiers stood on the hill dialing in the two resin cannons the commander was pleased with the outcome of the new weapons. The Empress’s new innovations have proved incredibly useful so far and he would have to send her a letter of complement he thought smiling as another salvo went down range.

They soldiers, now deafened from the loud report of the cannons, did not hear the whisp of the multitude of arrows as they arced into the encampment and to the commander’s horror almost half the troops collapsed with arrows in there backs and chest, as he was about to rally his troops towards the direction of the arrows, another salvo sprang from behind him taking another large swath of his troops, the cannons stood silent as the short dwarven came riding up over the small cover the soldiers had built to cover the cannons and the short horses they rode easily cleared it as the screaming dwarven slaughtered all that was left including the surprised commander who still sat atop his horse trying to figure out what just happened.

An hour later the Silvan troops returned the two cannon and a cart of blue crystal resin cannon balls in tow. Durass turned to Uri. “If there are more of these, we cannot stay here, I suggest we ride to Castello, it would be the safest place” Durass stated andUri nodding Gravely. Corliss who stood a short distance away cocked her head and Uri noticed her for the first time since the bombardment had started. “The capital of the Silvan people” he said.

It only took four hours to pack everything that hadn’t been destroyed, through they would have to leave the carts behind, the small cannons in tow and tents folded around the blue cannon balls dragged them behind horses as well as supplies and other items too heavy to carry. The entire procession made its way into the dense forest of the barrens the wardens leaving the territory of Vicor proper for the first time in their history as an organization.
